messages: elena: Heads-up — running the docs linkcheck and seeing consistent failures for anchors when a heading is immediately followed by an unordered list. Example broken link: /guides/serve#quick-setup resolves to an anchor like `quick-setup-1`. jason: Huh, haven't seen that exact pattern. Can you paste a tiny repro markdown file and the linkcheck output? elena: Sure — minimal repro below: ```markdown ## Quick setup - Install the package - Run `redwood serve` See also: [quick setup](#quick-setup) ``` Linkcheck output (snippet): `ERROR anchor not found: /guides/serve#quick-setup -> resolved to /guides/serve#quick-setup-1` priya: I think this is an MD slugging quirk when the heading text collides with list item IDs. Two quick options: add an explicit id on the heading (if attr_list is enabled) or insert an explicit HTML anchor above the heading. e.g. ```markdown ## Quick setup {#quick-setup} - Install the package - Run `redwood serve` ``` or ```html ## Quick setup - ... ``` jason: Good call. Which builder is this? MkDocs or Docusaurus? Behavior may differ. elena: MkDocs (mkdocs-material with python-markdown). The site was migrated recently and we turned on some extra markdown extensions. Might be attr_list is off in the new config. priya: If attr_list is off, enabling `markdown_extensions: [attr_list]` is the least invasive. Otherwise we can add a linter rule to prefer explicit IDs for headings that have list siblings. elena: I'll try enabling attr_list locally and re-run linkcheck. If that fixes it, I'll open a tiny PR to update mkdocs.yml and add a short note in the migration guide. jason: If you're short on time I can take the PR and handle the config test matrix (local build + CI linkcheck). ping me when you open it. docs-bot: linkcheck/job/472 started for branch: feature/docs-anchor-fix — status: queued :hourglass_flowing_sand: elena: Thanks — opening PR now, will add the repro page under `docs/testing/anchor-repro.md` and a changelog entry. Will tag @jason for reviews and @priya for migration notes. priya: Nice. Also consider adding one assertion to our linkcheck CI to fail if any anchor mismatch appears (so we catch regressions). elena: Good idea — I'll add that to the PR pipeline step. Thanks all :thumbsup:
